title: Portobello Bacon
cScaleSummary: C0 because the recipe contains no cholesterol-contributing animal-derived ingredients. The portobello mushrooms, soy sauce, olive oil, smoked paprika, balsamic vinegar, garlic powder, and black pepper contribute 0 mg cholesterol.
ldlActiveSummary: LDL-Active is false because this is a small seasoning component built for smoke, chew, and browned flavor rather than a legume-forward, fiber-forward, or otherwise LDL-lowering dish structure.
intro: Plant-based “bacon” works best when it stops trying to imitate pork exactly and focuses on the useful parts: smoke, salt, browning, chew, and savory depth. Portobello mushrooms are especially good for this because they have enough structure to dehydrate into flexible, dark, concentrated strips with crisped edges after a quick hot finish. This is a seasoning component, not a main dish, meant to add smoky chew and browned flavor to pasta, sandwiches, salads, bowls, and breakfast plates.
miseEnPlace: Prepare {{ingredient:portobello-mushroom-caps}} as specified: gills scraped, sliced into 1/4-inch strips.

stepGroups.title: Dehydrate the portobello bacon
items: Whisk together the soy sauce ({{quantity:soy-sauce}}), olive oil ({{quantity:olive-oil}}), smoked paprika ({{quantity:smoked-paprika}}), balsamic vinegar ({{quantity:balsamic-vinegar}}), garlic powder ({{quantity:garlic-powder}}), and black pepper ({{quantity:black-pepper}}).
Add the portobello strips ({{quantity:portobello-mushroom-caps}}) and toss gently until evenly coated.
Let the mushrooms stand for 10 minutes so the marinade can absorb.
Arrange the strips on dehydrator trays in a single layer, leaving space between pieces.
Dehydrate at 135°F until the mushrooms are darkened, reduced, leathery, and flexible, about 8 to 12 hours.
Store the dehydrated strips refrigerated until needed.

stepGroups.title: Re-crisp before serving
items: Re-crisp only the amount needed for the recipe.
Heat a dry skillet over medium heat and cook the strips for 2 to 4 minutes, turning occasionally, until the edges darken and lightly crisp.
Use immediately while the edges are crisp and the centers remain chewy.
